HYDERABAD TALUK

Chaitanyapurî.-- Engraved on a boulder locally known as Kosaguṇḍla Narasimhasvāmī in the village.
cells.remarks: Records the establishment of a dwelling (samāsa) by Bhadanta Samghadēva, the water-bearer of the gaṁdhakuṭī of Gōvindarāja-vihāra, who is described as the disciple of Bamhadēva-thavira of the lineage of Vāsudēva-Śiridāma, who is stated to have established the 'great vihāra, on the Puphagiri (i.e., Pushpagiri), and mahāpiṁdapātika Vāmadhara. In characters of the 5th century A.D. (Contra: JESI., Vol. XI, pp. 95-96, 1984).

cells.location: Baṭranpalle
cells.place: Stone lying near the dilapidated Jaina basadi outside the village.
cells.date: Cāḷukya Vikrama year 32, Sarvadhāri, Vaiśākha śu. 5, Thursday (Irregular).
cells.remarks: Registers the consecration of the Jaina image and the gifts of a mango-garden, 20 maṭṭars of keramba land and other lands for the renovation of the basadi and feeding of the ascetics by Bīramā-raḍḍi, the daṇḍanāyaka of Bhuvanagiri and the karaṇam of Bekkallu after laving the feet of Sēnaboṭṭadēva. Also records some more gifts to the same Jaina basadi by Punni-raḍḍi of Naṅganūru and Rēvi-raḍḍi of Baṭṭama-Paṭla and others. Ibid., No. 18.

cells.place:
WARANGAL DISTRICT--contd.

CHERIYAL TALUK--contd.

Bekkallu.-- Broken pillar lying in the compound of Śiva temple near a hillock.
cells.date: Cāḷukya Vikrama year 32, Sarvadhāri, Vaiśākha śu. 5, Thursday (Irregular).
cells.remarks: Introduces Rēvi-reḍḍi, his grandson Punni-reḍḍi and the latter's grandson Malli-reḍḍi, who is also referred to as Vekkaṇṭipuravarēśvara. Malli-reḍḍi is stated to have caused the construction of 21 temples for the merit of 21 generations preceding him and temples of trikūṭa and other types for his own merit and made some grants for worship in them. In characters of the 11th-12th century A.D. Ibid., No. 20.

cells.location: Ingurti
cells.place: Do. Stone lying in the compound of the Zilla Parishad High School.
cells.date: Śaka 1143=(Rām-ābhdhi=Rudra), Vṛiṣha, Vaiśākha [ba]30, Solar eclipse,Sunday=1221 A.D., May 23. (The month was Nija-Vaiśākha).
cells.remarks: Mentions Kākati Prōla, his son Mahādēva and also Buddhabhūpati. States that Mallamā of the Kākati family made gifts of clothes, cows, lands and flower gardens to god Śiva, probably in the temple caused to be constructed by her. This large temple complex consisted of a number of shrines, embellished with lofty tiers, steps and a portico (prāṅgaṇa). The temple is stated to have been embellished with beautiful sculptures including those of female musicians and paintings on either side of the shrine of Gōpālakṛiṣhṇa. Ibid., No. 59.

cells.location: Koravi
cells.place: Two broken pillars in the compound of Vīrabhadrasvāmi temple.
cells.remarks: In four parts. The first part states that Cālukya Bhīma was installed on the throne by Kusumāyudha after defeating Kannaraballaha. The second part mentions that Nitravādya succeeded his elder brother Goṇagayya on the throne and he, besides renewing all the endowments made earlier by his elder brother, set up a stone pillar recording this fact. The third part which, however, is incomplete refers to one Peddana, the son of Nalla Mēlēya of Koravi. The fourth part contains imprecations prescribing punishments on the nāyaka and kāmpus of the place who help the enemy. In characters of about the 10th century A.D. Ibid., No. 6.

cells.location: Muḍikkarai
cells.place: Vishnu temple, second beam in the maṇḍapa.
cells.date: Regnal Year 14 Mēsha 12, ba. 12, dvādaśī Sunday, Uttarāṭṭādi=1229 A.D. April 22. The Solar day was 29.
cells.remarks: Registers the sale of land for a price-value by an individual Chakravatti Tirukkāṇaperuḍaiyān alias Mālāvarāyan of Muḍikkārai in Tirukkāṇapper-kūrram in Pāṇḍi-maṇḍalam to Paṭṭi-Nārāyaṇan, a brāhmaṇa of Malai-maṇḍalam. Further it states that the kadamai accruing out of these kārāṇmai lands was to be given to the deity Uḍārapprivaiyāngaremurumān of Muḍikkārai for conducting the procession festival, on the day of the donor's birth star Uttiram. Among the boundaries of the land, a highway leading to Madurai is referred to.

cells.remarks: Incomplete. Commences with the praśasti Puvinkilatti, etc., of the king. States that the tiruviḍaiyāṭṭam lands from Cūḷāmaṇi-nallūr endowed to a brāhmaṇa named Udārapparuṁan of the village Maṅgalam became fallow on account of the damage to the tank, canal and due to the forest growth. It was regranted as kāṇi to the brāhmaṇas of the village to raise crops in order to meet the expenses of the services (tiruppaṇi) in the temple.

cells.language: Arabic and Persian, Tughra and Nasta'līq
cells.remarks: Muḥammad Shāh 'Ālam (I) Bādshāh Ghāzī (probably from her mother's side). States that Nawwāb Raf'at Sulțānu'z-Zamānī Begam died on the given date at the age of 14 years and 6 days. Further it traces the pedigree of the deceased from her mother side as : Daughter of late Nawwāb 'Umdatu'z-Zamānī Begam daughter of Mirzā Muḥammad Ra 'īs Bakht known as Shāhzāda Zubairu'd-Dīn Bahādur son of Mirzā Shāh Mirzā Dārā Bakht, the crown-prince, the first son of Ḥaḍrat Sulțān Abū'z-zafar Sirāju'd-Dīn Muḥammad Bahādur Shāh. Pedigree from her father's side is traced as : Daughter of Muḥammad Ibrāhīm Bakht son of Shāhzāda Muḥammad Mirzā son of late Mirzā Hājī, son of late 'Alījjāh Şāhib son of Ḥaḍrat 'Azīzu'd-Dīn 'Ālamgīr (II).

cells.location: Mikoḷ
cells.place: Loose marble slab in possession of Shri Moti Singh Sursingh Jhāla of the village.
cells.date: A.H. 1055 (and chronogram)=1645 A.D., February 17 - 1646 A.D., February 6.
cells.remarks: States that when Aurangzeb was the (governor) of Ṣūba (Province) of Gujarat, Hāj, the leader of the turbulent people rose in rebellion. Aurangzeb ordered Barkhurdār to chastise him. In the encounter that followed, Hāj was caught with his arms. It further states that Barkhurdār after his victory over this turbulent leader, erected this fort on the given date. The text was written by Hidāyatu'llāh Rīvī.
